description: ARTEMIS is a multidisciplinary team combining software development, AI, data analysis, UI/UX design, research, and creative storytelling. We aim to transform NASA data into an innovative, technically strong, and visually engaging solution with meaningful impact. We value curiosity, teamwork, and ambitious ideas.
summary:
ARTEMIS is an interactive website that takes students on a journey to the Moon and Mars. On the Moon, they can explore a device left by Apollo 11 and learn how scientists use it to measure the distance to the Moon. On Mars, they can follow the Opportunity rover, compare rock samples, and discover clues that water once existed there.

We built ARTEMIS to show that the equipment left in space still has stories to tell. By exploring and making discoveries for themselves, students can see how simple observations help scientists answer big questions.
details:
We built ARTEMIS: Echoes Beyond Earth, an interactive website that lets students explore real equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Visitors choose a destination, land on the surface, and inspect an object to learn what it did and why it matters.

On the Moon, students explore a device left by Apollo 11 and learn how it helps scientists measure the distance between Earth and the Moon. On Mars, they follow the Opportunity rover, compare two rock samples, and discover why tiny round grains gave scientists a clue about past water.

We wanted students to feel like explorers. Instead of reading a long page of facts, they can choose where to go, look closely at an object, and uncover the story behind it. We used simple language and short activities to make the science easier to understand. We also linked to NASA sources and marked our AI-generated scenes as illustrations.

We built the website with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, and published it on Vercel. The experience runs in a web browser and does not require special hardware.
